description: Small-business action guidance for proactive honeypot CTI. Rules are human-curated from cited trusted sources and should not be labeled as generated intelligence.
limitations: This policy turns honeypot evidence into prioritized guidance for non-specialist operators.
It does not prove that a production host was compromised.
Predicted next steps are likely or possible hypotheses and should be verified against real logs before major remediation.
Attempted commands and Cowrie login acceptance do not establish successful action or compromise of a real account.
Disruptive actions require corroboration from real-host or network telemetry and explicit operator approval.

automation_safety.rationale: Remote-access control changes can disrupt legitimate administration; an operator must approve them.

actions.action: Review source IP {src_ip} and apply temporary rate limiting or blocking only when repeated activity, reputation, or real-system telemetry corroborates risk.
actions.why: A single honeypot interaction is useful defensive context but is not sufficient by itself to justify a permanent block.
